parameters.content:
Court-notice reading for Dyzania LLP (fictional). Upload scans or photos; a vision model copies what is printed into JSON; the tested rules (the Code nodes, generated from the library) decide the priority. Every row is saved with the status "Needs attorney confirmation": nothing here, and nothing a document says, can approve a notice. Only a person changes that cell.
The code never works out a deadline. It repeats a date as printed and counts days only to decide who looks first. A time limit counted from another event is copied as printed.
Urgent (a summons or subpoena, a date within 7 days or already passed, a poor scan, a date that could not be read, or a failed read) sends ONE email per upload to the attorney on duty. The email has no party names. If the table row cannot be saved the email says so.
The upload form needs a basic-auth credential: notices are privileged. Execution data is not saved. Images go to a third-party model (see the README before using real papers). Each notice also writes one ops event (reference, type, priority and reason codes only), which the daily digest counts; a notice whose row could not be saved is logged as an error.
